title: Do not treat verified cross-marketplace predecessor performance as directly portable proof
scenario: A seller launches a closely equivalent product/keyword structure in JP using a verified business mapping from a mature US predecessor. The US entity was historically profitable and responded well to a bid increase. The request asks whether the JP successor can inherit the US bid and scaling conclusion.

forbidden_behaviors: Copy or currency-convert the US predecessor bid into the JP successor as an action-safe recommendation.
Treat the US Worked/Keep outcome as proof that the same bid direction or magnitude will work in JP.
Transfer US CPC, CVR, profitability thresholds, target economics, or validation state as JP current truth.
Reject all predecessor evidence merely because the marketplace changed; verified historical relevance or known failure modes may still be useful as hypotheses.
required_observations: The predecessor/successor relationship is verified, but cross-marketplace continuity is weaker than same-marketplace continuity.
Historical relevance, business intent, and known failure modes may transfer as bounded directional context, while bid magnitude and performance outcomes require JP-specific evidence.
Currency, auction conditions, demand, retail positioning, competition, and conversion economics can break direct portability even when targeting semantics are similar.
The JP successor needs its own mature baseline or controlled test before a performance-based scaling conclusion becomes action-safe.

rubric.requirement: Preserve both marketplace/profile scopes and classify the mapping as a cross-marketplace transition.
Allow only bounded portable context from the predecessor and reject cloning of performance outcomes or current state.
Recognize that currency and marketplace economics invalidate direct transfer of bid/CPC/CVR/profitability conclusions.
Use JP-specific evidence or an experiment before making an action-safe scaling recommendation.
